title: Monster telegraphs
_note: Foreshadowing hints for the dungeon bestiary (inline, no _default bucket — only these authored monsters get a hint). `monster` keys must EXACTLY match a member/elite name in data/monster-families.json or a lord boss name from js/ui/app.js's LORD_INTERIOR (Lich, Necromancer, Vampire, Dragon, Hag). Referenced by js/gen/bestiary.js.

telegraphs: Dry, rattling stillness — as if the room is holding its breath, waiting to fall in on itself.
A film of bone-dust lies undisturbed across the floor, except where things stood.
Something clatters faintly behind the walls whenever you go quiet.
An inscription over the door reads: "A silver sword, or remain forever."
The torches burn a sickly blue here and give no warmth.
Your shadow lags a half-step behind you as you cross the threshold.
Crude tally-marks and a gnawed bone are nailed above the door — a trophy, or a warning.
Giggling echoes somewhere close, cut off the moment you listen for it.
The smell of woodsmoke and unwashed fur drifts from just ahead.
Massive, silent footprints press deep into the dust — whatever made them didn't hurry.
A club-sized dent is punched clean through a nearby door.
The hairs on your neck rise before you hear anything at all.
Fresh tracks circle the passage twice before doubling back the way you came.
A low, chorus growl rolls through the dark just past the edge of your torchlight.
Bones, cracked for marrow, lie scattered in a loose ring.
Deep gouges rake the stone at chest height, clawed through as if it were wood.
The reek of wet feathers and old blood thickens the air.
Something enormous shifts its weight beyond the door, and the floor answers.
Silk threads, thick as rope, span the ceiling in a loose, deliberate weave.
Husks — leathery, drained, and man-sized — hang wrapped in a corner.
A faint clicking keeps time somewhere just out of torchlight.
A cloying, sweetish rot hangs in the air, thicker than the dungeon should allow.
Something glistens and slow-moving vanishes around the bend as you round the corner.
Half-dissolved bones lie in a puddle that has not dried in years.
Candle wax pools thick beneath a black-draped altar, still warm.
Chanting, low and unhurried, carries from somewhere below — in a language you don't recognize.
A ring of ash marks the floor, swept clean at its center like a stage.
The walls and floors here are unnervingly clean — scrubbed bare of grime, bones, even dust.
A faint acid tang hangs in an otherwise empty passage.
A single boot, half-dissolved, sits abandoned in the middle of the corridor.
A trail of etched, pitted stone marks a slow, wandering path down the hall.
The air smells faintly of vinegar where the passage narrows.
A discarded blade lies fused into the floor, its edge eaten to a nub.
Statues line the chamber in postures of sudden, frozen terror.
A veil hangs across the inner doorway, and no draft stirs it.
Something in the dark hisses softly, like dry grass in wind.
The stench of char and rot mingles here — old fire, older meat.
Claw-scored bones, snapped and regrown wrong, litter a crude nest.
A wound in the wall itself looks half-healed, knitting slowly closed.
The cold here is not the dungeon's cold — it has a will, and it is watching.
Every candle in the chamber burns black, and the flames cast no light.
A voice, dry as parchment, seems to read your thoughts back to you in fragments.
Fresh grave-dirt is tracked across otherwise ancient dust — someone, or something, was walked in recently.
Rows of bones lie sorted by size, awaiting purpose.
A ledger of names sits open on a lectern, half of them crossed out.
No mirror in the chamber holds a reflection of the room correctly.
Wine glasses, untouched, sit filled with something too dark and too thick.
The portraits on the wall are centuries old, and every face is the same.
The air shimmers with heat that has no visible source.
Coins, half-melted and fused together, glint at the passage's end.
A slow, rhythmic rumble vibrates up through the stone — breathing, if you listen.
A cauldron bubbles somewhere unseen, and the smell is almost, but not quite, appetizing.
Strands of hair — human, and not — are woven into the door's hinges.
A child's toy sits pristine and out of place amid the filth.
A slow, dragging scuff comes and goes beyond the wall — one foot, then the other, in no hurry at all.
The stench of spoiled meat rolls out to meet you before the room does.
Muddy handprints smear the walls at shoulder height, all of them reaching the same way.
Fresh-turned earth mounds in the corners, and something has been digging up, not down.
Bones lie cracked and sucked hollow, the tooth-marks too even to be an animal's.
A grave-cold hunger seems to wait in the dark, patient and very much awake.
Your torchlight falters here, guttering as if the dark itself leaned in to drink it.
The shadows on the wall do not quite match the things that cast them.
A creeping chill climbs your arms, and for a moment your own shadow will not follow.
The air turns grave-cold, and your breath hangs grey though nothing else stirs.
The torches dim to embers here, and no coaxing will bring them back.
A thin, mourning wail threads through the stone, always from the room you have not yet entered.
Dry, spiced dust coats everything — embalming resin, gone stale over centuries.
Strips of ancient linen lie shed across the floor, trailing toward a sealed inner door.
A curse is carved above the threshold, and the letters look freshly cut.
A cold that sinks past skin and into the marrow settles the moment you enter.
Frost rimes the walls of a room that has never known winter.
Something passes through the torchlight without breaking it, there and gone.
A suit of black plate stands at the room's end, and you cannot say whether it is empty.
The cold ring of a gauntlet closing on a hilt sounds once, deliberate, from the dark ahead.
Rotted banners hang on the walls, every one bearing a sigil scratched violently out.
The floor ahead bristles with clumsy tripwires and half-hidden snares.
Tiny clawed footprints crisscross the dust, far more of them than their size should leave.
A yipping, chattering squabble echoes down the tunnel, then falls guiltily silent.
Crude weapons and cracked shields lean against the wall like a war-band's spare kit.
The reek of sweat, smoke, and rancid grease hangs thick in the passage.
A guttural, barking song drifts from ahead, kept to a marching beat.
The camp ahead is ordered — bedrolls squared, weapons racked, a sentry-line drawn in chalk.
A watch-horn hangs by the door, and the floor is swept clear for a clean field of fire.
Bootsteps drill in unison somewhere close, then halt all at once.
The gnawed remains of something — someone — hang from a hook, half-butchered.
A high, broken laughter yips and cackles just past the edge of the torchlight.
The smell of a slaughterhouse thickens, wet fur and old blood together.
Something here reeks at once of grave-rot and wet hound — two stenches that should not share a body.
Claw-scored bones lie heaped in a nest, and the wounds on them have begun, impossibly, to close.
A shape lopes just beyond the light, and it does not move like any one creature should.
A crude throne of lashed bone and hide dominates the far wall, draped in stolen finery.
Trophies — helms, hands, teeth — hang in tallied rows, and the newest is still dripping.
The whole warren has gone silent, the way lesser things go quiet near something that eats them.
The walls seethe faintly, a dry rustle of fur behind every crack and gap.
Droppings and gnawed leather carpet the floor in a reeking, shifting mass.
Red pinprick eyes catch your torchlight from the low dark, dozens of them at once.
A shrill, needling squeak stabs at the edge of hearing, then circles behind you.
The dust is churned by small, frantic tracks that never once hold still.
Something small and ravenous darts across the passage, too fast to count.
The lower walls are scored with tusk-marks, gouged deep and waxy with old grease.
Rooting has torn the floor's debris into furrows and heaps.
A snuffling grunt and the stamp of a heavy hoof sound just past the bend.
A kill lies half-eaten and dragged into a corner, still faintly warm.
Deep claw-rakes streak a stone ledge worn smooth by a returning haunt.
The hair on your neck rises — something has been watching, unblinking, from above.
Tracks the size of your two hands press deep into the muck, spread in a hunting line.
A low, layered growl rolls out of the dark, too big and too many to place.
Bones lie splintered in a wide ring, cracked by jaws that could take a limb.
Gouges rip along the wall at chest height, the tusk-marks a hand's-breadth apart.
The floor is churned to a ploughed ruin, stones flung aside like pebbles.
A deep, chuffing snort answers your torchlight, and the ground trembles with it.
Claw-marks tower far above your reach, raked down through the living stone.
A rank, musky den-smell fills the passage, warm and animal and close.
Something vast shifts and settles in the dark ahead, and its breathing does not hurry.
The cracks in the walls glisten with a slick, restless movement.
Cast skins, long and many-legged, lie curled and brittle in the corners.
A dry, chittering ripple of countless legs whispers over the stone.
A pair of dim red glows bob in the dark ahead, cold and unhurried, going nowhere.
Husks with faintly luminous glands lie cracked open and scavenged.
The click and scrape of hard shells on stone ticks steadily from the black.
The ceiling is crusted thick with dried droppings and crumpled, bat-like husks.
A shrill whine of wings needles the air, closing and fading and closing again.
Small drained carcasses hang wedged in the rafters, pale and puncture-marked.
The walls seem to shift colour where you look, as if the stone itself were crouching.
Near-invisible silk threads part against your face in the doorway.
A drained husk lies wedged in a crevice, wrapped and sucked dry.
A low, seething hum rises and falls from every crack in the walls at once.
The floor and ceiling crawl with a restless dark carpet that never holds still.
The air itself feels thick and prickling, alive against your skin.
Deep, paired gouges drag a slow trail across the floor toward a crevice.
A dry, armoured clatter clicks somewhere close, then falls dead still.
A curled, barbed cast-off and chitinous husks lie shed in a dark alcove.
Cheap tallow candles burn in rows before a crude, hand-daubed idol.
A murmured, half-learned prayer stumbles on from somewhere ahead, over and over.
Incense hangs sweet and cloying, not quite masking something underneath.
Hooded robes hang on pegs by the door, still warm and smelling of smoke.
A many-voiced chant rises and falls beyond the wall, all of it in step.
A symbol you do not know is painted in dried red over every doorway.
The walls are scrawled with feverish scripture, the same line a thousand times over.
Dried blood crusts a whipping-post, the stains layered years deep.
A single voice cries out ahead in ecstasy or agony — you cannot tell which.
Weapons lie notched and blood-crusted, flung down where their rage burned out.
The walls bear dents at head height, punched by fists or by skulls.
A ragged, building roar answers your light, more beast than man.
Chalked circles and half-finished sigils cover the floor in careful, arcane rings.
The air prickles with a faint charge, and your hair lifts of its own accord.
Guttering candles burn in colours no honest flame should take.
An altar is cluttered with self-inflicted offerings — teeth, fingers, locks of hair.
Figures kneel in perfect rows ahead, and it is not clear that all of them still breathe.
A whispered oath repeats from the dark, promising an eager, joyful death.
A patch of the ceiling glistens a wet, vivid green, and it drips.
The stone beneath a slow ooze is pitted and eaten hollow.
A cleared circle of bare floor lies below it, scoured of everything that fell.
A stretch of wall shines slick and wet, though the stone around it is bone-dry.
What looked like a puddle of grease lies too still, and faintly rippling.
A dropped blade lies half-eaten into slag where it fell.
Every scrap of metal in the passage is pocked and flaking, crumbling to orange dust.
A discarded sword lies gnawed to a lace of rust, its edge gone entirely.
A feathery, questing feeler twitches from a crevice, tasting the air for iron.
A single strong filament, sticky and taut, stretches down from the dark above.
Drained husks hang wedged high on a ledge, wrapped and long since dry.
A faint clicking tracks your movement from somewhere overhead.
Stone figures crouch along the walls, and you cannot recall if that one faced you a moment ago.
Grit and stone-dust lie scattered beneath perches worn suspiciously smooth.
The statues' claws are chipped and scored, as though they had gripped and torn.
The walls are riddled with holes bored clean through the stone, at every angle.
Figures stand frozen mid-flight, mid-scream, mid-crumble — each struck by a different doom.
A prickling sense of being watched settles over you, from everywhere, all at once.
Skulls line a shelf, each cracked open cleanly at the crown and emptied.
A cold pressure builds behind your eyes, and a whisper that is not sound brushes your thoughts.
The air smells of brine and something colder, far deeper than any sea should reach.
The passage narrows, and every surface — walls, floor, ceiling — is scoured unnaturally clean.
Acid-etched channels run down the stone, dissolving handholds and steps alike.
A vast, glistening blackness fills the far end, and it is slowly spreading your way.
A line strung across the passage is rigged with a clatter of tin cups.
Cold ashes and picked-clean bones mark a rough camp, hastily struck.
Low, wary voices count something in coin, then hush at your step.
Looted packs lie slashed open and rifled, their owners nowhere in sight.
Crude threats are gouged into the wall beside a leering, painted grin.
A jeer and a whistle carry down the passage, passed from man to man.
Army-issue gear lies dumped in a heap, its unit-marks scratched away.
A watch-fire burns low and unwatched, no sentry at the post.
Hushed, frightened arguing breaks off the moment your light appears.
A body lies slumped in the shadows, its purse cut and its throat cut with it.
The passage offers a dozen blind corners, and every one of them feels occupied.
A boot scrapes stone behind you, though the room ahead is where you were looking.
The camp is neat and paid-for — matched gear, a tally of coin, a contract nailed to the door.
A crossbow rests loaded on a bipod, angled down the only approach.
A bored, professional voice calls a challenge before you round the corner.
The gear here is old, mended, and cared-for, every blade honed to a working edge.
Scars are notched into a tally-post beside a row of well-kept helms.
A calm, unhurried order to hold is spoken once, and obeyed at once.
A high-backed chair sits atop a heap of plundered goods, lording over the room.
A map of ambush-sites is pinned to the wall, marked in a confident hand.
One voice silences all the others ahead, plainly used to being obeyed.
Clusters of leathery eggs are tucked into the warm cracks along the walls.
A sticky patter of climbing feet crosses the ceiling and stops directly overhead.
Shed skins, papery and translucent, snag in the crevices.
Fish-bone fetishes and gutted river-catch litter a damp, muddy nest.
Webbed, clawed tracks lead in from a flooded passage and do not lead back out.
A low, hissing croak answers your torch, then another, spreading round the room.
An eye-watering reek, sharp as spoiled musk, floods the passage and will not lift.
The walls are smeared and daubed, and the stone itself seems to sweat the stench.
Pale, clammy handprints trail toward a crevice too dark to see into.
Wide, dragging belly-trails groove the dust between deep, splayed clawprints.
A shed skin the length of a man lies sloughed and curling in a corner.
A heavy, cold-blooded stillness holds the room, waiting for warmth to pass.
A broad, smooth furrow winds through the dust, looping back on itself.
A vast shed skin, translucent and seemingly endless, drapes from a high ledge.
Something thick slides over stone with a long, dry hiss that has no end.
Serpent-scale mosaics coil across the walls, worked with unsettling, patient care.
A dry, whispering hiss shapes itself almost into words just past understanding.
The air is close and hot, and something sweet and venomous hangs beneath it.
Small creatures stand frozen mid-stride throughout the room, stone to the last whisker.
A cracked statue of a man lies toppled, his face locked in a final flinch.
A low, dragging hiss and the scrape of claws circle just beyond the light — do not meet its eyes.
A crude firepit ringed with cracked, man-sized bones dominates the room.
A reeking heap of hides and half-gnawed carcasses serves some brute for a bed.
A dull, heavy thud of footfalls shakes grit from the ceiling, slow and enormous.
The passages here fork and double back, scored with horn-marks at every turn.
A snorting, bellowing breath echoes from somewhere in the maze, impossible to place.
Gnawed bones and rusted arms lie heaped where the lost were run down.
Two sets of grunts argue from ahead, talking over one another in the same rough voice.
A crude, enormous double-headed club has gouged twin dents down the wall.
The stench of a thing that has never once washed rolls out ahead of it.
Boulders lie stacked into a crude, house-high cairn against the far wall.
Footprints deep enough to trip in press into the stone floor.
A slow, rockslide rumble of movement answers your light, and dust sifts down.
A single vast chair faces the door, flanked by a heap of skulls, all cracked open at the top.
A club the size of a tree-trunk leans by the wall, worn smooth with long use.
A booming, one-noted mutter carries from ahead, and something huge turns toward the light.
A mitre and crozier rest on the high seat, and the seat is not empty.
Cowled figures kneel at a defaced altar, lips moving in a prayer run backwards.
A hymn drifts from the nave, sung by voices with no breath to carry it.
The cracked bell tolls once, though no rope was pulled.
